# PDF test fixtures (ticket 17)

Deterministically generated PDF samples for the backend PDF text-extraction tests.
Regenerate with:

```bash
python3 tests/fixtures/pdf/generate.py
```

The generator uses only the Python standard library plus the pypdf wheel vendored at
`backend/attachments/pdf/pypdf-6.21.0-py3-none-any.whl` (added to `sys.path` directly,
so no environment install is needed). pypdf's document `/ID` is pinned to a fixed
value, so repeated runs produce byte-identical files and regenerating never shows up
as a spurious diff.

## Expected behaviour

| Fixture | Pages | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text.pdf` | 2 | Page 1 text is exactly `PAGE_ONE_ALPHA`, page 2 exactly `PAGE_TWO_BETA`. Independent per-page literals, so a test can assert that reading page 1 never returns page 2's text. |
| `empty.pdf` | 1 | Valid page with no text. `extract_text()` returns `""`; use for the no-text branch. |
| `encrypted.pdf` | 1 | `is_encrypted` is true and reading without the password raises `FileNotDecryptedError`. With password `fixture-password` it decrypts and page 1 reads `SECRET_PAGE_ALPHA`. |
| `damaged.pdf` | – | Not a valid PDF; opening raises `PdfReadError` (`startxref not found`). |
| `many-pages.pdf` | 501 | Blank pages, all empty text. For page-count limits and per-page read budgets. |
| `partial.pdf` | 2 | Page count is readable as 2 and page 1 extracts `PAGE_ONE_ALPHA`, but reading page 2 raises `PdfReadError` (invalid content stream). Models the partially-parsed case. |

`partial.pdf` is a valid document whose page 2 content-stream bytes are overwritten
in place with invalid operators, at exactly the same length. Keeping the length
identical means the catalog, page tree and xref offsets stay correct — which is the
whole point: structure and page count remain readable while that one page fails.
An earlier approach that pointed page 2's `/Contents` at a non-stream object was
rejected because it silently extracted `""` instead of raising, which would not
exercise the partial-failure path.

Note that opening `encrypted.pdf` with `PdfReader(...)` does not itself raise; the
signal is `reader.is_encrypted`, or `FileNotDecryptedError` when reading pages.
